newsitem.title: UK: Grand Met sees H1 profit up despite pound.
newsitem.headline: Grand Met sees H1 profit up despite pound.

text.p: British food and beverage group Grand Metropolitan Plc said on Tuesday it expected its first-half profits to rise versus last year despite the pound's strength.

The company, which owns fast food chain Burger King, said the strengthening of the pound against the dollar by one cent could hurt the group's profits on translation by 4.0 million pounds ($6.5 million).
Grand Met said total underlying group profits in local currencies were well ahead of last year, but added that the sterling value of its overseas profits had been affected by the pound.
"We believe that the strong pound has been the main reason for the weakness of our share price in recent months," chairman George Bull told the group's annual general meeting.
He added that trading in the first four months of the firm's financial year had developed as expected.
Bull said the company's cash flow remained strong, with net debt expected to be below 2.5 billion pounds at the half year.
Regarding Burger King, Bull predicted the chain would continue to make progress in the U.S. despite price discount plans by rival chain McDonald's Corp.

"We also believe that any anticipated price differential between McDonald's and Burger King will not be as dramatic as initially reported as the new price levels for burgers are expected to apply only to combination meals," he said.
Bull added that overall spirits volumes at the firm's IDV operations were ahead in the first four months, with good volume growth in Europe and improved market conditions in the U.S.
Grand Met's shares rose 5.5 pence to 459 by 1200 GMT.
